clue.text: Cause to move, but only as a temporary measure

parts.note: to cause someone to do something is to make them do it
to shift is to move

explanation.surface: Someone gets a thing moving, but only as a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap arrangement used until something better comes along is a temporary measure.

clue.text: A sheepish creature is one of a well-known trio

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A timid creature belongs to a famous threesome.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the Three Musketeers in Dumas's novel, alongside Athos and Porthos.

clue.text: Person avoiding making a point raved wildly

parts.note: E is a point of the compass, east

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of raved are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone dodging the issue made a point by ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' is the anagram signal and E, an east compass point, goes in front; 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who evades is a person avoiding something, such as duty or tax.

clue.text: Crowds around international leader and gives a boost

indicators.note: around means the crowds surround the next piece

parts.note: hosts are great numbers, crowds

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of international is taken

explanation.surface: Crowds gather round an international star and lift him up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise it up, giving it a lift or boost.

clue.text: Blundered — took a meal outside on the windy side

indicators.note: outside means the meal goes around the other piece

parts.note: fed means ate a meal
the luff is the windward side of a ship or the forward edge of a sail

explanation.surface: A picnic in a gale went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Luff is a sailing term for the edge of a sail facing the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff a task is to bungle it, so fluffed means blundered.

clue.text: Out-of-the-ordinary police function

definitions.meaning: making an arrest is a job of the police

explanation.surface: Unusual police duties.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means striking, and also the act of taking someone into custody.

clue.text: Cosmetic promotion seen in viewer screen

parts.note: the eye is the organ one views with

indicators.note: seen in means the promotion appears inside the screen

parts.note: to screen a film is to show it
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A make-up advert is shown on a television.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured powder applied to the eyelids is a cosmetic.

clue.text: A right toff in a South American country!

parts.note: a toff is a gentleman, a gent

explanation.surface: A real swell abroad in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the large country in the south of South America with Buenos Aires as capital.

clue.text: Light inside by request

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the clue says

parts.note: per is Latin for by, as in 'per post'
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A light is placed indoors at someone's request.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request, especially one addressed to God.

clue.text: Strike a number with financial liabilities as extortionate

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
C is the Roman numeral for 100
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Someone in debt lashes out at a figure demanding money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone greedily grasping for money far beyond what is fair.

clue.text: The French interview a tenant

parts.note: les is the French plural 'the'
to see someone is to interview or meet them

explanation.surface: French officials question someone renting a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, which makes them a tenant.

clue.text: Fish to be taken with a rod, that's quite plain

parts.note: the pike is a predatory freshwater fish
a staff is a stick or rod

explanation.surface: An angler takes a fish with a rod, which seems simple enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' makes the word stand for something obvious and unadorned.

clue.text: Artist's fanciful representation of a watercourse

indicators.note: a fanciful version is a free rearrangement, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A painter's imaginative picture of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ARTIST gives the answer; the possessive 's adds no letter and 'of a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow channel of sea linking two larger bodies of water is a kind of watercourse.

clue.text: With reorganisation of station, be firm

indicators.note: reorganisation means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Even when the station is reorganised, stand your ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link; the letters of STATION and BE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means stubbornly unyielding, which is one sense of firm.

clue.text: Form certain to accept short setback with the start of term

indicators.note: to accept means to take the next pieces inside

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: setback means the short word is set backwards

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: the start is the first letter of term

explanation.surface: A form is sure to take a brief hitch at the beginning of term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' reverses the word for short, 'the start of' takes the T of term, and 'to accept' puts both inside the word for certain. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure is the shape or arrangement of something, its form.

clue.text: Finding a party about over, left

indicators.note: about means the party goes around the next piece

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people
done means finished, over

explanation.surface: Arriving to find a party nearly finished and everyone gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been left behind or deserted.

clue.text: Reckon on a clergyman joining

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree

explanation.surface: Someone counts on a vicar coming on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to count up figures, that is, to total them.

clue.text: A social worker in Victorian times

indicators.note: in signals the answer lies within the run of letters

explanation.surface: A welfare worker of the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect lives in colonies and toils for them, so it is a social worker.

clue.text: Boring prohibitionist

definitions.meaning: one who supports a ban on alcohol

explanation.surface: A tedious teetotal campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dull, and also someone who wants alcohol banned.

clue.text: A cake, but not of soap

definitions.text: A cake, but not of soap

parts.words: A cake, but not of soap
parts.note: a cake of soap is a bar used in the tub; this is an edible cake named after a spa city

explanation.surface: A cake that is not soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a spa city in the west of England; its sticky sugared buns share a name with something you might find in a bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet sugar-topped yeast bun from the city of Bath is the cake meant, playing on bath soap.

clue.text: Smuggle staple food up the Mersey

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
corn is a staple grain

explanation.surface: Smugglers carry grain up the river into Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river of Liverpool in north-west England; Runcorn is a town on its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cheshire town lies on the River Mersey, upstream of Liverpool.

clue.text: What every child wants at Christmas — trifle

definitions.text: What every child wants at Christmas
definitions.meaning: a plaything is the classic Christmas present for a child
to trifle with is to play idly or not take seriously

explanation.surface: Every child wants a sweet dessert for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaything is a child's gift, and to dally or play idly with something is to trifle.

clue.text: Blase and far from satisfactory employee

parts.note: food that is off is bad, far from satisfactory
a hand is a worker, as in farm hand

explanation.surface: An indifferent and poor member of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual and unconcerned, which is what blase means.

clue.text: This is played away from school

definitions.text: This is played away from school

parts.words: This is played away from school
parts.note: reads like an away fixture for the school team, but means skipping lessons, in the idiom with 'play'

explanation.surface: A school match fixture away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: To play truant is to stay away from school without permission.

clue.text: Think much of always having serving men around

indicators.note: around means the serving men surround the other piece

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of serving soldiers
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always admires their servants.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in high regard, to think much of them.

clue.text: Swear when attending the big match!

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a Test is a full international cricket match

explanation.surface: Cursing while at the big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare solemnly or bear witness, that is, to swear.

clue.text: The cleaner president

definitions.meaning: a vacuum cleaner, after the brand name

explanation.surface: A president who is cleaner than others.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brand of vacuum cleaner, and the surname of the 31st US president.

clue.text: Love making complaint

definitions.meaning: an old medical sense: a disease or disorder affecting a part of the body

explanation.surface: Lovemaking leads to grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fondness, and in older medical usage a condition or disorder of the body.

clue.text: The country's not in a mess!

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a mess means jumbled up, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A national boast that the country is not in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' does double service in the surface but the fodder is NOT IN A, shuffled by 'mess'.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a state or people, which is what a nation is.

clue.text: Say so long as one can forget about work for a while

definitions.text: one can forget about work for a while
definitions.meaning: to go on a holiday from one's job

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye before a holiday from work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to bid farewell, and also to go off on holiday from one's job.

clue.text: Painter might appear a twister

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ..., the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A painter might seem a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the surname of the English Romantic painter, and also one who rotates or twists things.

clue.text: The risk coming with running water

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Danger arrives with a flood of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciting and hazardous undertaking is a venture involving risk.
